papers.title: ALFA: Agglomerative Late Fusion Algorithm for Object Detection
papers.review: Read abstract,introduction and methodIII.A/III.B including equations2-9 and renderedpage3. Already combines IoU and normalized full class-score Bhattacharyya affinity,complete-link clustering,one output per object hypothesis and class-score aggregation. Cross-class geometric/semantic late fusion is prior art. Candidate64affinity arm borrows BC only,not a faithful ALFA reproduction. Same-site directionalcontrast remains narrow and unproven,not an originality claim.

papers.title: Learning non-maximum suppression
papers.review: Abstract and4.1 loss: competing detections, one detection per object, earlier Hungarian matching-loss work and score-ordered benchmark-matching binary targets. Competition-aware detection scoring and matching-derived positive/negative labels are established. Relational scoring or adding a matching algorithm is not novel by itself.

papers.title: FUSEye: Training-Light Fisheye Detection with Overlapping Views and Zero-Initialized Adapters
papers.review: AgreeFusion paragraph before/after Figure3: descending-score fixed-seed clusters use still-unassigned detections, IoU>=.5, distinct-view support, cluster scoring and final NMS. Disjoint greedy clusters already prevent a detection from being reused across clusters. Distinct-view support counting is explicit prior art. Candidate47 must beat ordinary exclusive greedy allocation, not just unrestricted support.

novelty_boundary: Classdistribution affinity,multiview grouping,competition-aware scoring,NMS are established. Fixed directional class evidence at shared native sites versus independent-site maxima is a narrow design difference requiring actual deployment superiority and wider close-prior audit. Deterministic mathematical formula alone is not innovation.
